title: Career Roadmap · Surveyor
summary: A Surveyor measures land, boundaries, elevations and construction sites, producing accurate maps and survey data for infrastructure, buildings, roads, utilities and land development.

blocks.label: Recommended
blocks.text: Class 10 for the ITI Surveyor pathway; Science and Mathematics are useful for further technical study.

blocks.label: Stream
blocks.text: Science with Mathematics supports diploma and degree alternatives; exact eligibility depends on the course.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Geometry, maps, coordinates, levelling, land measurement and construction drawings.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Measurement accuracy, spatial reasoning, outdoor safety and basic computer skills.

blocks.label: Stage 1 — Foundation
blocks.text: Geometry, scales, coordinates, levelling and measurement.

blocks.label: Stage 2 — Core skills
blocks.text: Use surveying instruments, take field measurements and maintain field books.

blocks.label: Stage 3 — Advanced skills
blocks.text: Total station, GNSS/GPS surveying, CAD mapping and GIS fundamentals.

blocks.label: Stage 4 — Career preparation
blocks.text: Complete supervised fieldwork, check measurement accuracy and prepare survey plans.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Survey a small plot • Prepare a site-level plan • Create a contour map from sample data • Convert field measurements into a CAD drawing.

blocks.text: Eligible public works, land-survey, infrastructure and technical departments.

blocks.label: Private
blocks.text: Surveying contractors, civil engineering consultancies, road and construction firms, GIS companies.

blocks.text: Land measurement • Levelling • Total-station operation • Survey drafting and mapping.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Construction, roads and highways, railways, land development, mining, utilities, infrastructure consultancy and geospatial services.
Government survey posts may have separate recruitment, qualification and licensing rules.

blocks.label: Technical skills
blocks.text: Levelling, triangulation concepts, coordinates, field-book recording, measurement checks, site safety and survey-data interpretation.

blocks.label: Tools / technologies
blocks.text: Auto level, theodolite, total station, GNSS/GPS receivers, AutoCAD and GIS software.
Useful credentials
Choose training that includes supervised practical fieldwork; software certificates alone do not establish surveying competence.

blocks.label: Countries to explore
blocks.text: Canada, Australia, UK, Germany and New Zealand.
Institutions / routes to investigate

items.text: BCIT — Canada; geomatics and surveying-related programs.
TAFE providers in Australia — surveying and spatial-information courses.
UK colleges / universities — surveying, geomatics and land-related programs.
German universities of applied sciences — geodesy, geomatics or surveying.
New Zealand tertiary providers — surveying and spatial-science programs.

blocks.label: Common requirements
blocks.text: Academic records, language proficiency where applicable, subject prerequisites and program-specific practical or portfolio requirements. Verify current international admissions and course availability on official institution websites.

blocks.label: Roles
blocks.text: Survey Technician, Land Survey Assistant, Engineering Survey Technician, Geomatics Technician and GIS Technician.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Construction, infrastructure, mining, utilities, land development and geospatial services.
Professional land-surveyor licensing rules differ by country and may require additional education, supervised experience or examinations. Employment and visa sponsorship are not guaranteed.
